rows.sub: In 1983, builders in Guangzhou, in southern China, struck a sealed stone tomb. It belonged to a king of Nanyue, a lost kingdom claimed by both Chinese and Vietnamese history.
rows.say: In 1983, builders in Gwahng-joe, in southern China, struck a sealed stone tomb. It belonged to a king of Nahn-yweh, a lost kingdom claimed by both Chinese and Vietnamese history.

rows.sub: He lay in a suit of more than two thousand jade plates, sewn together with silk thread.
rows.say: He lay in a suit of more than two thousand jade plates, sewn together with silk thread.

rows.sub: On his body lay a gold seal with a coiled dragon. Its inscription reads: seal of Emperor Wen.
rows.say: On his body lay a gold seal with a coiled dragon. Its inscription reads: seal of Emperor Wen.

rows.sub: But the Han histories call this man a king, King Wen of Nanyue. A king in the books. An emperor in his own tomb.
rows.say: But the Han histories call this man a king, King Wen of Nahn-yweh. A king in the books. An emperor in his own tomb.

rows.sub: His grandfather, Zhao Tuo, was a Qin officer from the north. Vietnam's first national chronicle made him an emperor of its own. Later Vietnamese historians called him an invader.
rows.say: His grandfather, Jow Twaw, was a Chin officer from the north. Vietnam's first national chronicle made him an emperor of its own. Later Vietnamese historians called him an invader.

rows.sub: So whose kingdom was Nanyue? Let's look at what the sources actually say.
rows.say: So whose kingdom was Nahn-yweh? Let's look at what the sources actually say.

rows.sub: Around 214 BC, armies of the Qin, the first Chinese empire, pushed south across the mountains.
rows.say: Around 214 BC, armies of the Chin, the first Chinese empire, pushed south across the mountains.

rows.sub: Qin set up three new commanderies there: Nanhai, Guilin and Xiang.
rows.say: Chin set up three new commanderies there: Nahn-hye, Gway-lin and Shyahng.

rows.sub: Convicts and settlers were sent to live among the local peoples, whom the Chinese called the Yue.
rows.say: Convicts and settlers were sent to live among the local peoples, whom the Chinese called the Yweh.

rows.sub: One of the northern officers was Zhao Tuo, from Zhending in the north. Qin made him magistrate of Longchuan, a county of Nanhai.
rows.say: One of the northern officers was Jow Twaw, from Jun-ding in the north. Chin made him magistrate of Long-chwahn, a county of Nahn-hye.

rows.sub: Then rebellions broke out in the north. The dying commander of Nanhai, Ren Xiao, called Zhao Tuo to his bed.
rows.say: Then rebellions broke out in the north. The dying commander of Nahn-hye, Ren Shyow, called Jow Twaw to his bed.

rows.sub: According to Sima Qian, Ren told him that Panyu, guarded by mountains and the sea, could be the heart of a state.
rows.say: According to Suh-mah Chyen, Ren told him that Pahn-yoo, guarded by mountains and the sea, could be the heart of a state.

rows.sub: Zhao Tuo took command. He closed the mountain passes, cut the new roads, and replaced Qin officials with his own men.
rows.say: Jow Twaw took command. He closed the mountain passes, cut the new roads, and replaced Chin officials with his own men.

rows.sub: When Qin collapsed, he took Guilin and Xiang as well, and around 204 BC named himself King of Nanyue. His capital was Panyu, today's Guangzhou.
rows.say: When Chin collapsed, he took Gway-lin and Shyahng as well, and around 204 BC named himself King of Nahn-yweh. His capital was Pahn-yoo, today's Gwahng-joe.

rows.sub: Who were the Yue? Not one nation. Chinese writers used the word for many southern peoples, the Hundred Yue.
rows.say: Who were the Yweh? Not one nation. Chinese writers used the word for many southern peoples, the Hundred Yweh.

rows.sub: Chinese texts describe Yue people who cut their hair short and tattooed their bodies.
rows.say: Chinese texts describe Yweh people who cut their hair short and tattooed their bodies.

rows.sub: In 196 BC, the new Han emperor sent an envoy south: Lu Jia.
rows.say: In 196 BC, the new Han emperor sent an envoy south: Loo Jyah.

rows.sub: Sima Qian says Zhao Tuo received him with his hair in a southern bun, sprawling with his legs stretched out.
rows.say: Suh-mah Chyen says Jow Twaw received him with his hair in a southern bun, sprawling with his legs stretched out.

rows.sub: Lu Jia scolded him. You are a man of the Central States, he said. Your family graves are in the north.
rows.say: Loo Jyah scolded him. You are a man of the Central States, he said. Your family graves are in the north.

rows.sub: Zhao Tuo sat up. I have lived among the southern peoples so long, he said, that I have forgotten my manners.
rows.say: Jow Twaw sat up. I have lived among the southern peoples so long, he said, that I have forgotten my manners.

rows.sub: Then he laughed. I did not rise up in China, he said, so I am king here. Had I been there, why would I be any less than the Han?
rows.say: Then he laughed. I did not rise up in China, he said, so I am king here. Had I been there, why would I be any less than the Han?

rows.sub: His court mixed northern settlers with Yue nobles. And Sima Qian lists Panyu as a rich market for pearls and rhinoceros horn.
rows.say: His court mixed northern settlers with Yweh nobles. And Suh-mah Chyen lists Pahn-yoo as a rich market for pearls and rhinoceros horn.

rows.sub: Lu Jia gave him a Han seal as King of Nanyue, and Zhao Tuo agreed to serve Han as a vassal.
rows.say: Loo Jyah gave him a Han seal as King of Nahn-yweh, and Jow Twaw agreed to serve Han as a vassal.

rows.sub: Then, under Empress Lü, Han officials banned the sale of iron goods to Nanyue at the border markets.
rows.say: Then, under Empress Lyoo, Han officials banned the sale of iron goods to Nahn-yweh at the border markets.

rows.sub: Zhao Tuo blamed the neighbouring king of Changsha. He declared himself Emperor of Nanyue and attacked Changsha's border towns.
rows.say: Jow Twaw blamed the neighbouring king of Chahng-shah. He declared himself Emperor of Nahn-yweh and attacked Chahng-shah's border towns.

rows.sub: Han sent an army. Heat and disease stopped it at the mountains. When the empress died, in 180 BC, the war ended.
rows.say: Han sent an army. Heat and disease stopped it at the mountains. When the empress died, in 180 BC, the war ended.

rows.sub: Han records say Zhao Tuo then used his army and his wealth to bring neighbours under his sway, including the Western Ou and the Luo.
rows.say: Han records say Jow Twaw then used his army and his wealth to bring neighbours under his sway, including the Western Oh and the Lwaw.

rows.sub: In 179 BC, the new emperor Wen repaired Zhao Tuo's family graves in the north, and sent Lu Jia south again.
rows.say: In 179 BC, the new emperor Wen repaired Jow Twaw's family graves in the north, and sent Loo Jyah south again.

rows.sub: Zhao Tuo wrote back as your old servant, great chief of the barbarians. He had called himself emperor, he wrote, only to amuse himself.
rows.say: Jow Twaw wrote back as your old servant, great chief of the barbarians. He had called himself emperor, he wrote, only to amuse himself.

rows.sub: But Sima Qian adds a quiet line. Inside his own kingdom, Zhao Tuo kept the old title. A king to Han. An emperor at home.
rows.say: But Suh-mah Chyen adds a quiet line. Inside his own kingdom, Jow Twaw kept the old title. A king to Han. An emperor at home.

rows.sub: Decades later, his grandson was buried with a seal that said exactly that. Emperor.
rows.say: Decades later, his grandson was buried with a seal that said exactly that. Emperor.

rows.sub: What about the Red River, in today's northern Vietnam? Here, two kinds of record tell different stories.
rows.say: What about the Red River, in today's northern Vietnam? Here, two kinds of record tell different stories.

rows.sub: For this region, the Han histories only name the Western Ou and the Luo, won over with gifts and the threat of an army.
rows.say: For this region, the Han histories only name the Western Oh and the Lwaw, won over with gifts and the threat of an army.

rows.sub: Many historians connect the Luo with the Lạc of the Red River plains.
rows.say: Many historians connect the Lwaw with the Lahk of the Red River plains.

rows.sub: Vietnamese tradition tells a story instead, written down many centuries later.
rows.say: Vietnamese tradition tells a story instead, written down many centuries later.
rows.src: LEGEND · Lĩnh Nam chích quái · Toàn thư (1479)

rows.sub: The legend says King An Dương of Âu Lạc built a spiral citadel at Cổ Loa. A golden turtle gave him a claw, to make the trigger of a magic crossbow.
rows.say: The legend says King Ahn Zuong of Oh Lahk built a spiral citadel at Koh Lwah. A golden turtle gave him a claw, to make the trigger of a magic crossbow.

rows.sub: With it he could not be beaten. So Zhao Tuo made peace, the story goes, and sent his son Trọng Thủy to marry the king's daughter, Mỵ Châu.
rows.say: With it he could not be beaten. So Jow Twaw made peace, the story goes, and sent his son Chong Twee to marry the king's daughter, Mee Chow.

rows.sub: Trọng Thủy secretly swapped the claw, then went home. Zhao Tuo attacked, and the crossbow failed.
rows.say: Chong Twee secretly swapped the claw, then went home. Jow Twaw attacked, and the crossbow failed.

rows.sub: The king fled with Mỵ Châu, who left goose feathers for her husband to follow. At the sea, the turtle named her the enemy, and the king killed her.
rows.say: The king fled with Mee Chow, who left goose feathers for her husband to follow. At the sea, the turtle named her the enemy, and the king killed her.

rows.sub: Even the date is disputed: around 208 BC in the Vietnamese chronicle, around 180 BC in many modern accounts.
rows.say: Even the date is disputed: around 208 BC in the Vietnamese chronicle, around 180 BC in many modern accounts.

rows.sub: Archaeology adds something else. Cổ Loa is real: huge earthen walls, the oldest layers from around 300 BC.
rows.say: Archaeology adds something else. Koh Lwah is real: huge earthen walls, the oldest layers from around 300 BC.

rows.sub: Digs found bronze arrowheads, and stone moulds to cast them. That shows a strong local power. It does not prove the legend.
rows.say: Digs found bronze arrowheads, and stone moulds to cast them. That shows a strong local power. It does not prove the legend.

rows.sub: Most historians think Nanyue ruled the Red River through local lords.
rows.say: Most historians think Nahn-yweh ruled the Red River through local lords.

rows.sub: Zhao Tuo died in 137 BC. The Vietnamese chronicle says he lived to a hundred and twenty-one, a number we cannot check.
rows.say: Jow Twaw died in 137 BC. The Vietnamese chronicle says he lived to a hundred and twenty-one, a number we cannot check.

rows.sub: His grandson took the throne, the king from the tomb. The histories call him Zhao Hu. His own seal says Zhao Mo.
rows.say: His grandson took the throne, the king from the tomb. The histories call him Jow Hoo. His own seal says Jow Maw.

rows.sub: When Han asked him to come to court, his ministers warned: go, and you will never come back. He stayed home, pleading illness.
rows.say: When Han asked him to come to court, his ministers warned: go, and you will never come back. He stayed home, pleading illness.

rows.sub: His son Yingqi, Sima Qian says, hid away the old seal of Zhao Tuo. The one that said Emperor.
rows.say: His son Ying-chee, Suh-mah Chyen says, hid away the old seal of Jow Twaw. The one that said Emperor.

rows.sub: Yingqi had married a woman from Handan, in the north. Their young son became king, and she became queen mother.
rows.say: Ying-chee had married a woman from Hahn-dahn, in the north. Their young son became king, and she became queen mother.

rows.sub: Han envoys came again. One, Sima Qian says, had once been her lover.
rows.say: Han envoys came again. One, Suh-mah Chyen says, had once been her lover.

rows.sub: The queen mother and the young king asked to join Han, under Han law.
rows.say: The queen mother and the young king asked to join Han, under Han law.

rows.sub: The minister Lü Jia, trusted by the Yue, refused. He told the kingdom the queen was a woman of the Central States, ready to hand its treasures to Han.
rows.say: The minister Lyoo Jyah, trusted by the Yweh, refused. He told the kingdom the queen was a woman of the Central States, ready to hand its treasures to Han.

rows.sub: In 112 BC, he killed the king, the queen mother and the Han envoys, and put another prince on the throne.
rows.say: In 112 BC, he killed the king, the queen mother and the Han envoys, and put another prince on the throne.

rows.sub: Emperor Wu sent armies and river fleets south. In the winter of 111 BC, Panyu burned and surrendered.
rows.say: Emperor Wu sent armies and river fleets south. In the winter of 111 BC, Pahn-yoo burned and surrendered.

rows.sub: Nanyue became nine Han commanderies. Three of them, Jiaozhi, Jiuzhen and Rinan, lay in what is now northern and north-central Vietnam.
rows.say: Nahn-yweh became nine Han commanderies. Three of them, Jyow-jir, Jyoh-jun and Ree-nahn, lay in what is now northern and north-central Vietnam.

rows.sub: Five generations, ninety-three years, Sima Qian counts. Then the kingdom was gone.
rows.say: Five generations, ninety-three years, Suh-mah Chyen counts. Then the kingdom was gone.

rows.sub: So whose kingdom was it? Each side has its own answer, and the answers have changed over time.
rows.say: So whose kingdom was it? Each side has its own answer, and the answers have changed over time.

rows.sub: To Sima Qian, Nanyue's kings were Han vassals, and 111 BC meant the Yue lands were finally settled.
rows.say: To Suh-mah Chyen, Nahn-yweh's kings were Han vassals, and 111 BC meant the Yweh lands were finally settled.

rows.sub: In Vietnam, the story began differently. In 1272, Lê Văn Hưu wrote the first national chronicle, and began it with Zhao Tuo, as Triệu Vũ Đế.
rows.say: In Vietnam, the story began differently. In 1272, Lay Vahn Hew wrote the first national chronicle, and began it with Jow Twaw, as Chee-oh Voo Day.

rows.sub: He praised him for opening up our Việt land and standing up to the Han.
rows.say: He praised him for opening up our Vee-et land and standing up to the Han.
rows.src: Lê Văn Hưu, in Toàn thư

rows.sub: In the eighteenth century, the scholar Ngô Thì Sĩ disagreed. Zhao Tuo ruled from Panyu, he argued, as a foreign king.
rows.say: In the eighteenth century, the scholar Ngoh Tee See disagreed. Jow Twaw ruled from Pahn-yoo, he argued, as a foreign king.

rows.sub: Many twentieth-century Vietnamese historians followed that line. Zhao Tuo became an invader, and King An Dương the ruler who lost to him.
rows.say: Many twentieth-century Vietnamese historians followed that line. Jow Twaw became an invader, and King Ahn Zuong the ruler who lost to him.

rows.sub: In Guangzhou, the tomb is now a museum, and Nanyue is presented as the region's own heritage, the culture of Lingnan.
rows.say: In Gwahng-joe, the tomb is now a museum, and Nahn-yweh is presented as the region's own heritage, the culture of Ling-nahn.

rows.sub: Modern historians, like Keith Taylor and Erica Brindley, point to a problem with all of these answers.
rows.say: Modern historians, like Keith Taylor and Erica Brindley, point to a problem with all of these answers.

rows.sub: Around 200 BC, there was no China or Vietnam as we know them. Yue was an outsider's word for many peoples, and Nanyue was a mixed kingdom.
rows.say: Around 200 BC, there was no China or Vietnam as we know them. Yweh was an outsider's word for many peoples, and Nahn-yweh was a mixed kingdom.

rows.sub: A northern family ruled it, through southern lords. Later nations each read their own story into it.
rows.say: A northern family ruled it, through southern lords. Later nations each read their own story into it.

rows.sub: Nanyue did not quite disappear. Its name came back, two thousand years later.
rows.say: Nahn-yweh did not quite disappear. Its name came back, two thousand years later.

rows.sub: In the early 1800s, the new Nguyễn ruler Gia Long asked the Qing court to recognise his kingdom as Nam Việt.
rows.say: In the early 1800s, the new Nwin ruler Zah Long asked the Ching court to recognise his kingdom as Nahm Vee-et.

rows.sub: Qing records show the court objected. Ancient Nanyue had covered Guangdong and Guangxi, lands now part of the Qing.
rows.say: Ching records show the court objected. Ancient Nahn-yweh had covered Gwahng-dong and Gwahng-shee, lands now part of the Ching.

rows.sub: So in 1804 the two words were turned around. The country became Việt Nam.
rows.say: So in 1804 the two words were turned around. The country became Vee-et Nahm.

rows.sub: A Nanyue king's jade suit now lies in a Guangzhou museum. And the name of his lost kingdom lives on, reversed, in the name of a country.
rows.say: A Nahn-yweh king's jade suit now lies in a Gwahng-joe museum. And the name of his lost kingdom lives on, reversed, in the name of a country.

rows.sub: Was Nanyue Chinese, Vietnamese, or neither? Tell us what you think in the comments, and subscribe to Rice and Empires.
rows.say: Was Nahn-yweh Chinese, Vietnamese, or neither? Tell us what you think in the comments, and subscribe to Rice and Empires.

tl.caption: Nanyue, about 204–111 BC (early dates differ by source)
